solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepare by boiling for two months

parts.note: December is shortened to Dec
October is shortened to Oct

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: simmer this for a full two months.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two months' are not a cooking time but two abbreviated month names, December and October, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to extract the essence of something by boiling it down.

clue.text: Belittle blue entertainment

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down, low in spirits
a play is a theatrical entertainment

explanation.surface: Sneering at a risqué show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue entertainment' suggests smut, but blue here means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to make it seem less important, to minimise it.

clue.text: Go away when it's cloudless on holiday

parts.note: a clear sky has no clouds
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: Heading off on vacation once the weather is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order to leave, meaning depart.

clue.text: Wrath possibly shown by head

definitions.meaning: the far north-western tip of the Scottish mainland is named for it, an example of a headland
a promontory jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Anger displayed by a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrath' reads as anger, but it is a place name: Cape Wrath is a headland in the far north-west of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a promontory, and Wrath is one famous example.

clue.text: Picadors get injured now and then

indicators.note: the picadors being hurt signals that the letters of the word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Bullfight horsemen are occasionally hurt in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adverbial while the answer is an adjective; read it as 'occurring now and then'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic happens occasionally and irregularly, at scattered intervals.

clue.text: Chap splits drinks with us — bags of them

indicators.note: the chap breaks into the pair of drinks, coming between them

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
tea is a hot drink
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow pours out drinks for the group, with plenty of luggage around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags of them' sounds like 'lots of them', but bags are suitcases; 'of them' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag that opens into two halves.

clue.text: One's case may rest on it

definitions.text: One's case may rest on it

parts.words: One's case may rest on it
parts.note: sounds like a lawyer resting a case, but a suitcase sits on a luggage shelf

explanation.walkthrough: The legal phrase 'rest one's case' is a decoy; the case is luggage on a luggage shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack is a framework or shelf for holding things such as bags on a train.

clue.text: Run to make the Five Ten

definitions.meaning: to go at a quick pace, as soldiers ordered to move at speed
multiplying five by two gives ten

explanation.surface: Hurrying so the Famous Five become ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to move at a run and to multiply by two.

clue.text: Be the first to make a fuss?

definitions.meaning: to bring something into being for the first time
informally, to complain loudly or kick up a row

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to be the first to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to originate something and, informally, to make a scene.

clue.text: Warm start aids pups

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from warm

parts.note: to aid someone is to help them, so aids gives helps

explanation.surface: Some warmth at the outset helps young dogs along.
explanation.definitionFit: Whelps are the young of a dog, so the word is a synonym for puppies.

clue.text: Leave out one note in introductory piece

indicators.note: the note is placed in the middle of the introductory piece

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece of music
C is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A musician is told to omit a note from the opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out or exclude it, a synonym for leaving out.

clue.text: Its main trade is in disarray, control required

indicators.note: being in disarray means disordered, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: A firm's core business is in chaos and needs regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or govern something, a synonym for control as a verb.

clue.text: A bit of leave

definitions.meaning: a portion or piece of a whole
to go away from someone, as when friends separate

explanation.surface: A little of a holiday allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a piece of something and to separate or go away.

clue.text: Watership Down author gives female manuscript

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: The writer of Watership Down hands over a woman's manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Adams wrote the rabbit novel Watership Down, published in 1972.

clue.text: Fifty caught in a bit of a fiddle

definitions.text: Fifty caught in a bit of a fiddle

indicators.note: being caught in something means being trapped inside it, so the fifty sits within the string

parts.note: violin strings were traditionally made of catgut, so gut is part of a fiddle
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty notes are found stuffed inside part of a violin, or a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate definition: the whole clue is meant to picture an excess, fifty items crammed into something as thin as a string, while 'fiddle' also hints at a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty crammed into a slender string is an overabundance, a surplus beyond what fits.

clue.text: Dig out a story that makes the headlines

definitions.meaning: to remove by hollowing out with a spoon-like tool

definitions.text: a story that makes the headlines
definitions.meaning: an exclusive news story one paper gets first

explanation.surface: A journalist digs up a front-page tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to hollow out and also a newspaper exclusive.

clue.text: Tried to get a seat — unsuccessfully apparently

definitions.text: Tried to get a seat — unsuccessfully apparently

parts.words: Tried to get a seat — unsuccessfully apparently
parts.note: a candidate in an election runs for a seat; someone who failed to find a chair on a train was left upright

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a seat' means winning election to parliament; the joke is that a person who could not find a chair also ended up on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To run in an election is, in British usage, to stand for a seat.

clue.text: Showing love to fat fianceé in a strange way

indicators.note: behaving strangely suggests the letters of those words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone behaves oddly but fondly towards a plump fiancée.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate person displays warmth and fondness towards others.

clue.text: Pay attention and watch this space

parts.note: to watch is to look
here means in this place or spot

explanation.surface: A command to be alert, as in a newspaper teaser promising more to come.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a call demanding someone's attention, often as a mild rebuke.

clue.text: Any power may resort to producing armaments

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Any nation may turn to making weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort to' looks like turning to something; read it as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is a collective word for weapons, the same as arms.

clue.text: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?

definitions.text: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?

parts.words: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?
parts.note: read playfully, the phrase is a time at which one may not lose, so winning must come at once

explanation.surface: A sporting moment when a quick win is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom normally means 'hurry up'; the clue reads its last word literally, as a moment where defeat is not an option.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means there is a pressing need for haste, matching the urgency of a quick win.

clue.text: Wear a well-trimmed beard

indicators.note: a beard that has been well trimmed has been reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sporting neatly groomed facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear' looks like putting on the beard, but it means to rub away.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear down a surface by friction.

clue.text: Crazy man let loose

indicators.note: letting the letters loose frees them to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A madman has been set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental is an informal word for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Grouse meat

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to complain, and a complaint is a grievance
flesh from cattle eaten as food

explanation.surface: Game bird served up as the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird, which fits with 'meat', but here it means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a complaint and the flesh of cattle.

clue.text: A full-bodied drink

definitions.meaning: describing someone heavily built or plump
a dark, strong beer brewed with roasted malt

explanation.surface: Describing a rich, heavy beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a portly person and is also a dark kind of beer.

clue.text: Miss spring

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over something

explanation.surface: A young woman named alongside a season.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to leave something out and to jump lightly.

clue.text: Employs sources of inspiration to clear head

indicators.note: clearing the head means removing the first letter of the word

parts.note: the Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspired the arts

explanation.surface: Using inspiring ideas to clear one's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to employ it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Past get-up a Roman wore

indicators.note: in a down clue the hyphenated up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the past tense of get is got

explanation.surface: Describing a costume from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-up' looks like a costume, but splits: 'Past get' is GOT, and '-up' turns it round in this down entry. The definition is elliptical: what a Roman wore.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose woollen robe was the dress of citizens in ancient Rome.

clue.text: It pushes up water rates in a reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation rearranges things, so the letters of the three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A utility company's restructuring forces water bills upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushes up water rates' reads as bills rising; the definition stops at 'water'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well forces groundwater up under natural pressure, so the word names such a source.

clue.text: Show progress? Don't exaggerate!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'get away with you'

explanation.surface: A sceptical reply to someone boasting of their improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to improve and is also a cry of disbelief at an overstatement.

clue.text: Came into force

parts.note: reads as a law taking effect, but means joined the armed forces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Came into force' normally describes a law taking effect; here 'force' means a military service that someone signed up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to join the forces.

clue.text: Seldom depend on the Gunners

indicators.note: one piece placed on another in a down-style ordering: the word for depend comes after, set on the gunners

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
to depend on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: One can hardly ever count on the artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means not often, a direct synonym.
